correlation_memo: Seven of eleven names (AGIO, SVRA, ANNX, AQST, CAPR, DBVT, OLMA) load on ONE shared factor - FDA/clinical risk-on/off plus biotech beta - the same factor as the named cluster (BBIO/AQST/ZYME/VRDN/EYPT/CELC/AMLX/VIR). Their resolution events are separate decisions, but their marks and their failure gaps move together on FDA posture and XBI (a peer biologic's refusal letter last weekend coincided with CAPR -12% and SVRA -4.4% on 16 Nov, with no news at either). Seating three of them (AGIO, SVRA, ANNX) is ONE bet: hold the three together to about one standard seat, SVRA smallest because it resolves first (Fri 20 Nov) and its floor is deepest. AGIO is the least-beta member - nearly half its price is net cash and the rest an approved, revenue-earning franchise - so it carries the cluster's core weight. The other four names are more independent but not driver-free: KBR (Trinzic's notes, financing-cost driver) and FLEX (Axiom = AI-capex AND financing-cost drivers, about 1.8 beta) share the breached credit tape with each other, and NFG rides gas prices next to the breached energy/Hormuz driver. The purest standalone asymmetries are DDL - a China SAMR decision on a signed cash sale, with a floor mostly in cash at a Cayman parent, uncorrelated with FDA posture, US credit, AI-capex or oil (its one overlay is US-China politics; the truce runs to 10 Jan) - and, inside the FDA lane, AGIO, whose loss leg is bounded by cash rather than by biotech sentiment. KBR is the next most independent: its downside is a conglomerate multiple, not a binary.
